values.value: • Do not become complacent just because there is no visible competitor today. • Confirm whether the real competitor is delay, internal build, or status quo. • Use the opening to lock decision criteria, buying path, and timeline. • Build preference before a new competitor enters the picture. • Keep momentum and do not over-negotiate against yourself.
9|No competition
Buyer may say, 'We are not comparing right now.' Response: 'Good to know. Then my focus will be on helping you make a clean decision, not on forcing a competitive pitch.'
Do not relax. Use the open lane to shape the buyer criteria and lock the path to decision.
Low risk. Create decision momentum.
Ask: 'Since you are not comparing active options, what would help you feel fully confident moving ahead?'
No competition

• Use competitive weakness to sharpen your differentiation early. • Make the buyer say what matters most and tie those points to your strengths. • Show why your approach is safer, faster, easier, or more outcome-driven. • Prevent the discussion from becoming only price-based. • Use proof and relevance to close the door on weaker alternatives.
9|Yes, but weak
Buyer may say, 'We are speaking to someone else too.' Response: 'That makes sense. Let me focus on the few areas where the decision will really be made, not on broad claims.'
Differentiate early and make the comparison easy. Show why choosing you is safer, simpler, and more useful.
Risk: Weak competition can still win if you stay generic.
Say: 'Let me show where we will create better outcomes with less execution risk.'
Yes, but weak

• Build a deliberate competitive plan instead of hoping your proposal speaks for itself. • Understand why the competitor is strong: relationship, pricing, product, incumbent status, or perception. • Attack where you are truly stronger and avoid fighting on their best ground. • Equip the buyer with a clear reason to choose differently. • Bring internal leadership or specialists if the deal is strategically important.
9|Yes, they are strong
Buyer may say, 'The other vendor is very strong here.' Response: 'Understood. Then it becomes important that I show you where our approach is genuinely stronger for your priorities.'
Stop feature dumping. Build a win story around buyer pain, proof, access, and what the competitor cannot match.
Risk: Strong competitor needs a sharp counter-plan.
Ask: 'What would make you choose the safer partner here, not just the familiar one?'
Yes, they are strong

• Find out who else the buyer is considering and how they are being judged. • Ask whether this is a formal comparison, incumbent renewal, or market scan. • Understand the competitor's hold on the account, if any. • Without competitive clarity, you cannot choose the right sales strategy. • Do this before proposal if possible.
9|Don't know
Buyer may say, 'We are still deciding who all to look at.' Response: 'That helps. I would still like to understand what alternatives you may compare so I can stay relevant to your evaluation.'
Find out who else is in, what they are known for, and how the buyer is comparing options. You need a real battlefield map.
High risk: No competitive picture.
Ask: 'Who else is being considered, and what do you think they are strongest at in this deal?'
Don't know
Are there any competitors on this deal ?
